messages.subject: Spatially varying coefficient survival model
parts:
Hello,

I am experimenting with fitting a spatially varying coefficient survival model. In order to the SVC, I used the formula (generic) below. I got a result and was able to visualise it but I am uncertain about the approach; considering the data is at the individual level and not the spatial unit level.

form <- inla.surv(time, status) ~ 1 + f(id, pm2.5, model = "besag")

Is the formula or approach above correct? if not, how can I capture spatial heterogeneity
or svc in my survival model?

Thank you,

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatially varying coefficient survival model
parts:
On Tue, 2021-11-09 at 08:59 -0800, Prince Michael Amegbor wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I am experimenting with fitting a spatially varying coefficient
> survival model. In order to the SVC, I used the formula (generic)
> below. I got a result and was able to visualise it but I am uncertain
> about the approach; considering the data is at the individual level
> and not the spatial unit level.
>
> form <- inla.surv(time, status) ~ 1 + f(id, pm2.5, model = "besag")

this seems correct. please have in mind that the sum of 'id' would be
zero by default for model="besag", hence, it would be more natural to
add

f(id, pm2.5, mode="besag", scale.model=TRUE, constr=FALSE)

to remove the sum to zero constraint (and to scale the model at the same
time).

even if you have individual data, you have the pm2.5 measurement
attached to it as a proxy for the exposure, and it make sense to be.

>
> Is the formula or approach above correct? if not, how can I capture
> spatial heterogeneity
> or svc in my survival model?
>
> Thank you,
